summary: The RTSP localhost MVP is substantially implemented and local unit/build checks pass, but the live feature is uncommitted, full-tree type/lint/browser gates are open, and Phase 10 protocol implementations have correctness, security, and acceptance gaps.

findings.title: The branch does not contain the reviewed live implementation
findings.trigger: A clone, CI run, deployment, or handoff checks out live-video-search.
findings.guard: Commit the reviewed source and rerun mandatory acceptance on that clean revision.
findings.consequence: The branch reproduces only the file-video baseline.

findings.title: HLS policy enforcement stops after one playlist snapshot
findings.trigger: A master playlist, refreshed media playlist, segment, or key introduces a later URI or redirect.
findings.guard: Continuously mediate, validate, and rewrite the complete dynamic graph before FFmpeg can fetch it.
findings.consequence: FFmpeg can request destinations that were never checked by the source allow policy.

findings.title: Literal-IP HLS binding breaks HTTPS and virtual-host routing
findings.trigger: An HLS endpoint relies on TLS SNI, hostname certificate validation, or an HTTP Host header.
findings.guard: Pin network resolution while preserving application-layer hostname identity.
findings.consequence: Valid allowlisted production HLS streams fail.

findings.title: URL reconstruction drops query parameters
findings.trigger: A source requires a signed token or input option in its query string.
findings.guard: Preserve the validated private query while redacting it from public provenance.
findings.consequence: Signed HLS and parameterized camera URLs fail at connection time.

findings.title: Authenticated HLS fails during credential-free preflight
findings.trigger: The playlist itself requires structured username/password credentials.
findings.guard: Authenticate the private policy fetch and define safe redirect credential behavior.
findings.consequence: Advertised HLS credentials are unusable for protected playlists.

findings.title: SRT listener admission checks the bind endpoint instead of the peer
findings.trigger: An SRT listener accepts an incoming publisher.
findings.guard: Enforce actual remote peer identity at the gateway, firewall, or accept callback.
findings.consequence: Legitimate listeners can fail while an unapproved connected peer is never evaluated.

findings.title: SRT passphrases are not validated or safely encoded
findings.trigger: A passphrase has an unsupported length or contains control characters.
findings.guard: Enforce the SRT passphrase contract, reject controls, and use an injection-safe transport.
findings.consequence: Real connections fail or secret content changes the ffconcat script.

findings.title: Source PATCH accepts protocol-incompatible transports
findings.trigger: A source transport is changed to a value its protocol cannot use.
findings.guard: Reuse create-time protocol/transport validation before persistence.
findings.consequence: The API stores configurations that fail asynchronously during validation or capture.

findings.title: Most FFmpeg code-1 failures reconnect forever
findings.trigger: FFmpeg returns code 1 for persistent auth, input, codec, protocol, or option errors.
findings.guard: Classify transient errors narrowly and enforce a durable total retry/time budget.
findings.consequence: Permanently invalid sources consume resources in an endless degraded loop.

findings.title: Partial delete-by-query can remove media for surviving documents
findings.trigger: Elasticsearch reports fewer deleted documents than requested.
findings.guard: Inspect failures and verify each chunk is absent before media reclamation.
findings.consequence: A searchable result can survive after its clip and thumbnail are deleted.

findings.title: Age-delete combines a large single request with partial execution
findings.trigger: The candidate cap is exceeded or many IDs share one backing index.
findings.guard: Stop before mutation on truncation, persist continuation, and use bounded delete batches.
findings.consequence: Cleanup can be partially destructive and can exceed practical request limits.

findings.title: Protect ranges race with age-delete
findings.trigger: A protect range is created after cleanup snapshots protections.
findings.guard: Serialize protect mutations with destructive jobs or recheck protection atomically at deletion.
findings.consequence: Newly protected data can still be deleted.

findings.title: Application E2E cleanup evidence is optimistic and incomplete
findings.trigger: Cleanup fails, is interrupted, or leaves run-created chunks/events/handles.
findings.guard: Check responses, wait terminal, report actual outcomes, and assert no active run-owned resources.
findings.consequence: Evidence claims cleanup even while durable test state remains.

findings.title: Strict readiness omits documented completion gates
findings.trigger: Strict readiness runs without browser, application-path, standalone type, or lint checks.
findings.guard: Add every documented mandatory gate to one exact-PASS clean-revision aggregate.
findings.consequence: Strict readiness can succeed while declared completion checks remain open.

findings.title: Phase 10 checkmarks do not satisfy the planned acceptance contract
findings.trigger: Offline adapter tests are interpreted as completed protocols.
findings.guard: Run protocol-specific disconnect, timestamp, auth, redaction, image-capability, gateway, and remote acceptance.
findings.consequence: Eight stubbed tests are treated as proof of three live transport implementations.

findings.title: The WHIP example grants anonymous publish and API access
findings.trigger: An operator copies the example onto a reachable gateway.
findings.guard: Use explicit secret-backed identities and bind management locally.
findings.consequence: Any reachable client can replace the camera path or invoke the gateway API.

findings.title: HLS capability probing is not enforced
findings.trigger: HLS is enabled on a worker image without required FFmpeg capabilities.
findings.guard: Gate HLS source readiness on the capability manifest and test the actual image.
findings.consequence: A source becomes ready and then enters a capture failure loop.

findings.title: The worker container remains unpinned and root
findings.trigger: The image is rebuilt or FFmpeg processes hostile media.
findings.guard: Pin dependencies and use a non-root, reduced-capability, read-only runtime.
findings.consequence: Builds drift and a media parser receives unnecessary privilege.

findings.title: Dirty evidence hashing includes volatile and generated files
findings.trigger: Untracked tmp caches or review manifests are present.
findings.guard: Use a clean commit or a reviewed immutable source inclusion manifest.
findings.consequence: The hash depends on irrelevant bytes and is not a practical reproducible source identity.

findings.title: Known runtime limits remain deferred
findings.trigger: A source changes codec/audio/PTS or retained-media caps are enabled.
findings.guard: Implement fragment probing/epoch changes and retained-media eviction with acceptance tests.
findings.consequence: Windows can cross discontinuities and configured caps do not reclaim retained bytes.

findings.title: Current status is contradictory across primary documents
findings.trigger: A maintainer tries to determine current completion state.
findings.guard: Use one evidence-backed status block and mark older present-tense reports historical.
findings.consequence: Phase 10 simultaneously appears next, closed, open, and implemented.

findings.title: Protocol wording overstates what the code enforces
findings.trigger: Readers interpret re-validation, peer admission, and WHIP adapter literally.
findings.guard: Describe one-time preflight, listener-address checking, and internal RTSP subscription precisely until stronger mechanisms exist.
findings.consequence: Documentation creates false security and capability expectations.

verification_gaps.title: Phase 10 tests never run a real protocol
verification_gaps.evidence: Tests inject DNS/fetch stubs and inspect script text only.

verification_gaps.title: HLS tests omit dynamic graph, TLS, query, and auth cases
SRT tests do not verify caller or listener behavior
verification_gaps.evidence: No real SRT peer, disconnect, timestamp, or capable image run.

verification_gaps.title: WHIP has no browser or publisher test
verification_gaps.evidence: Only an internal RTSP URL is validated.

verification_gaps.title: Age-delete tests omit partial Elasticsearch responses and races
verification_gaps.evidence: Tests cover complete success, paging, and total failure only.

verification_gaps.title: Production build does not cover failing test-source types
verification_gaps.evidence: Build passes while standalone TypeScript emits 36 diagnostics.

verification_gaps.title: Browser completion remains unenforced
verification_gaps.evidence: Operations says NOT RUN and strict gate list omits Browser E2E.

verification_gaps.title: Cleanup reporting has no postcondition assertion
verification_gaps.evidence: Requested IDs are recorded as cleaned without checking response status or terminal state.

review_boundary: Application code was not changed. External Elastic and media services were not started or mutated.
